subject.title: Feature: Dynamic header templating for custom LLM providers (enables Fireworks.ai prompt caching)

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic runtime placeholder contract for provider headers, or keep session-aware request metadata limited to provider-specific affinity flags and explicit typed mappings?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the public config syntax, allowed runtime identifiers, privacy/security policy, and overlap with active narrower PRs require maintainer intent before implementation.

options.title: Approve narrow explicit placeholders
options.body: Support only approved placeholders such as {{session.key}}, {{agent.id}}, and {{run.id}} in provider/request headers, with docs and tests preserving static and SecretRef behavior.

options.title: Prefer typed affinity or mapping hooks
options.body: Keep configured headers literal and solve common cases through provider-specific compat flags or a typed provider request-metadata seam.

options.title: Defer for privacy design
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers define which runtime identifiers may leave OpenClaw and how users opt in.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow explicit placeholders
recommendation.body: Support only approved placeholders such as {{session.key}}, {{agent.id}}, and {{run.id}} in provider/request headers, with docs and tests preserving static and SecretRef behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Takhoffman is the live assignee and best available owner for the product/security boundary decision.
